stem: When you create a new table inside a scoped application, what does ServiceNow prepend to the table's name?

options.text: The application scope identifier, such as x_acme_myapp
The letter u followed by an underscore
The creating user's ID and a timestamp
The name of the parent table in full

distractor_notes.B: u_ is the prefix convention for custom tables and fields created in the global scope, not scoped apps.
distractor_notes.C: ServiceNow never names tables after the user or the time of creation.
distractor_notes.D: Extending a table does not rename the child table after its parent.

rationale: Tables and fields created inside a scoped application automatically receive that scope's prefix (x_<company>_<app>), which keeps scoped artifacts namespaced and protected.

stem: You need a custom table that inherits the fields and process behavior of the Task table. What is the correct approach?

options.text: Extend the Task table when defining the new table
Recreate every Task field manually on a new base table
Add Task as a related list on your new table
Create a reference field that points to Task

distractor_notes.B: Recreating fields by hand loses inheritance and the shared Task behavior and workflow.
distractor_notes.C: A related list links records but does not inherit fields or behavior.
distractor_notes.D: A reference field associates two records; it does not inherit the parent's fields.

rationale: Extending Task makes the new table a child in the Task hierarchy, inheriting its fields, business logic, and platform features such as SLAs and assignment.

stem: Which statement best describes an application file in ServiceNow?

options.text: A record that belongs to and is tracked by an application
A binary attachment stored on the app record
The XML produced when an app is published
A file written to the instance operating system

distractor_notes.B: Application files are configuration records, not binary attachments.
distractor_notes.C: Published XML is an export artifact, not the definition of an application file.
distractor_notes.D: Application files live in the database, not on the host file system.

rationale: An application file is any configuration record (table, business rule, UI policy, and so on) that is associated with and version-tracked by its application.

stem: A developer in the global scope tries to edit a script include that belongs to a scoped app and is blocked. What most likely controls this?

options.text: Cross-scope access settings on the scoped application
The developer's missing admin role
A read-only field on the script include form
An active update set in the wrong state

distractor_notes.B: Admin rights do not override scope protection; cross-scope rules still apply.
distractor_notes.C: A read-only field would limit one field, not block editing a scoped artifact.
distractor_notes.D: Update set state controls capture, not cross-scope edit protection.

rationale: Scope protection and cross-scope privileges govern whether code in one scope can modify artifacts in another; the scoped app must grant access for outside edits.

stem: Where do you set the default number format (prefix and starting value) for records on a custom table?

options.text: The Number Maintenance record for the table
A field default value on the form
The table's dictionary label entry
A UI policy on the number field

distractor_notes.B: A field default sets a value but not the auto-incrementing number sequence.
distractor_notes.C: The dictionary label controls display text, not numbering.
distractor_notes.D: UI policies change field state, not number generation.

rationale: Number Maintenance (sys_number) defines the prefix, number of digits, and next number for a table's auto-generated record numbers.

stem: Which tool makes a field mandatory or read-only on a form without writing code?

options.text: UI Policy
A Client Script using g_form calls
A Business Rule on the table
An ACL write rule

distractor_notes.B: A Client Script can do this but requires scripting g_form methods.
distractor_notes.C: Business Rules run server-side and don't directly control form field state.
distractor_notes.D: ACLs restrict access; they don't set mandatory or read-only behavior.

rationale: UI Policies declaratively set fields mandatory, read-only, or visible based on conditions, with no scripting required.

stem: Which client script type runs as a form first loads in the browser?

options.text: onLoad
onSubmit
onChange
onCellEdit

distractor_notes.B: onSubmit runs when the form is submitted, not at load.
distractor_notes.C: onChange runs when a specific field value changes.
distractor_notes.D: onCellEdit runs when a list cell is edited inline.

rationale: An onLoad client script executes when the form renders, making it the place to set initial field state in the browser.

stem: You must hide a field on the form only when a checkbox is selected, with no scripting. What do you use?

options.text: A UI Policy with a condition and a Hide action
A before Business Rule that clears the field
An ACL that denies read on the field
A data policy on the table

distractor_notes.B: A Business Rule changes data server-side; it can't show or hide a form field.
distractor_notes.C: An ACL denies access broadly and isn't condition-driven on the form.
distractor_notes.D: Data policies enforce data rules and mirror to UI policies, but the direct UI control here is a UI Policy.

rationale: A UI Policy evaluates a condition on the form and applies field actions such as Visible = false, giving codeless show/hide behavior.

stem: What does a UI Action let an application developer add to a form or list?

options.text: A button, link, or context-menu item that runs logic
A new column on the underlying table
A scheduled background job
A read restriction on a field

distractor_notes.B: Adding a column is a dictionary change, not a UI Action.
distractor_notes.C: Scheduled jobs run on a timer, unrelated to UI Actions.
distractor_notes.D: Field read restrictions are ACLs, not UI Actions.

rationale: UI Actions add interactive controls (buttons, links, context-menu items) to forms and lists and run client or server logic when clicked.

stem: A field should default to the current user when a record is created through the form. Which is the simplest configuration?

options.text: Set the field's default value to javascript:gs.getUserID()
Write an onSubmit client script to set it
Add a business rule that updates it after insert
Use a UI Policy to populate the field

distractor_notes.B: An onSubmit script works but is more effort than a dictionary default.
distractor_notes.C: An after-insert rule sets it later and adds overhead versus a default.
distractor_notes.D: UI Policies change field state, not default values.

rationale: A dictionary default value with a javascript: expression (gs.getUserID()) populates the field automatically on new records without extra scripts.

stem: Which feature controls which fields appear, and in what order, on a form?

options.text: Form layout (Form Designer)
Access Control rules
The table's number maintenance
A scheduled data import

distractor_notes.B: ACLs control access to data, not which fields a form displays.
distractor_notes.C: Number Maintenance defines record numbering, not form layout.
distractor_notes.D: Imports load data; they don't arrange form fields.

rationale: Form layout, configured in the Form Designer, determines which fields are placed on a form and their arrangement.

stem: Different groups of users should see different fields on the same record. What is the recommended way to achieve this?

options.text: Create form views and assign them per group or context
Build a separate table for each group
Delete fields the group should not see
Add a client script that reloads the page

distractor_notes.B: A separate table per group fragments data and is unnecessary.
distractor_notes.C: Deleting fields removes them for everyone, not per group.
distractor_notes.D: Reloading the page does not change which fields display.

rationale: Form views let you present different field layouts of the same record to different audiences without duplicating data.

stem: In what order does ServiceNow evaluate ACLs for a record operation?

options.text: Most specific (field) to most general (table)
Table first, then field, alphabetically
Random order until one passes
Newest ACL first by creation date

distractor_notes.B: Field-level matches are evaluated before broader table-level rules, not after.
distractor_notes.C: ACL evaluation is deterministic, not random.
distractor_notes.D: Creation date does not determine ACL evaluation order.

rationale: ACL processing checks the most specific matching rule first (field-level), then the table level; the user must pass the matching rule that applies.

stem: What two things must a user satisfy for an ACL rule to grant access?

options.text: The required roles and the rule's condition/script
Only an admin role on their account
Membership in any group on the instance
A matching UI Policy on the form

distractor_notes.B: Admin bypasses many ACLs but is not the general requirement an ACL defines.
distractor_notes.C: Group membership alone does not satisfy an ACL's role and condition checks.
distractor_notes.D: UI Policies affect form fields, not ACL evaluation.

rationale: An ACL grants access only when the user holds the required roles and the rule's condition and script both evaluate to true.

stem: Users in a scoped app can read records they should not. Where do you look first to restrict read access?

options.text: The record (row) and field read ACLs for the table
The form layout for that table
The table's number maintenance record
A UI Policy on the form

distractor_notes.B: Form layout changes display, not who can read the data.
distractor_notes.C: Number Maintenance controls numbering, not access.
distractor_notes.D: UI Policies affect field state on the form, not data access.

rationale: Read access is governed by record and field-level read ACLs; tightening those rules controls who can see the rows and fields.

stem: What is the effect of granting a role the elevated 'admin' privilege?

options.text: It can bypass most ACL checks across the platform
It only grants access to the System Logs
It restricts the user to read-only access
It applies only inside a single application scope

distractor_notes.B: Admin is far broader than log access.
distractor_notes.C: Admin grants broad write access, not read-only.
distractor_notes.D: Admin is platform-wide, not limited to one scope.

rationale: The admin role can bypass most access controls, which is why it is granted sparingly and elevated privileges are used carefully.

stem: You want to allow read but block write on a field for most users. Which ACL configuration fits?

options.text: A field-level write ACL that requires a specific role
A table-level read ACL set to none
A UI Policy making the field read-only
A business rule that aborts the form

distractor_notes.B: Denying table read blocks viewing the record entirely, not just writing the field.
distractor_notes.C: A UI Policy is a client-side convenience and not true security.
distractor_notes.D: Aborting in a business rule is heavy-handed and not field-scoped access control.

rationale: A field-level write ACL requiring a role lets unauthorized users still read the field while preventing them from writing it; UI policies are not a security boundary.

stem: Which tool helps you see exactly which ACL allowed or denied an operation during testing?

options.text: The security/ACL debug (Debug Security Rules)
The system dictionary
The form designer
Number maintenance

distractor_notes.B: The dictionary defines fields, not ACL outcomes.
distractor_notes.C: The form designer arranges fields and shows no ACL traces.
distractor_notes.D: Number Maintenance is unrelated to security debugging.

rationale: Debug Security Rules outputs which ACLs were evaluated and their results, making it the go-to tool for diagnosing access issues.

stem: A scoped application needs another scope to call one of its Script Includes. What must be configured?

options.text: Cross-scope access privileges allowing the call
An admin role on every caller
A public UI Page in the target scope
A new role added to the caller's profile

distractor_notes.B: Admin does not bypass scope protection for cross-scope script access.
distractor_notes.C: A UI Page is unrelated to allowing cross-scope API calls.
distractor_notes.D: Adding a role does not grant cross-scope execution privileges.

rationale: Cross-scope access controls (and the Script Include's accessible-from setting) determine whether code in another scope may call it.

stem: In Flow Designer, what starts a flow running?

options.text: A trigger
A subflow
An action step
A data pill

distractor_notes.B: A subflow is reusable logic that a flow calls; it doesn't start the flow.
distractor_notes.C: Actions are the steps a flow runs after it starts.
distractor_notes.D: Data pills carry values between steps; they don't start flows.

rationale: A trigger defines the event or schedule that starts a flow, such as a record created or updated, or a timer.

stem: Which automation runs logic on a recurring schedule rather than in response to a record change?

options.text: A Scheduled Job (scheduled script execution)
A Business Rule triggered on update
An onChange Client Script
A UI Action button on the form

distractor_notes.B: Business Rules run in response to database operations, not on a timer.
distractor_notes.C: Client Scripts run in the browser when fields change, not on a schedule.
distractor_notes.D: UI Actions run when a user clicks them, not on a recurring schedule.

rationale: A Scheduled Job (scheduled script execution) runs on a defined recurring schedule, making it the right tool for periodic background automation.

stem: You need to run automation only when an incident's priority changes to 1. What trigger and condition fit best?

options.text: An Updated trigger with a condition on Priority
A Created trigger with no condition
A scheduled trigger that runs hourly
A REST trigger from an external system

distractor_notes.B: A Created trigger fires on new records, not on a priority change.
distractor_notes.C: A schedule runs on time, not in response to the field change.
distractor_notes.D: A REST trigger responds to inbound calls, not internal updates.

rationale: An Updated record trigger with a condition (Priority changes to 1) runs the flow precisely when that change occurs.

stem: When should you build a custom Action rather than inline flow steps?

options.text: When the logic should be reusable across flows
When the logic runs only once in one flow
When you want to avoid using Flow Designer
When you need to change a form layout

distractor_notes.B: One-off logic doesn't need to be packaged as a reusable action.
distractor_notes.C: Custom actions are part of Flow Designer, not an alternative to it.
distractor_notes.D: Form layout is a UI concern, unrelated to actions.

rationale: Custom Actions encapsulate steps with defined inputs and outputs so they can be reused across many flows, unlike one-off inline steps.

stem: A flow must call an external REST API as one of its steps. What is the standard way to do this?

options.text: Use an IntegrationHub spoke or REST action
Write the call in a UI Policy
Add the URL to the form layout
Create a number maintenance record

distractor_notes.B: UI Policies run in the browser and don't make server integrations.
distractor_notes.C: Form layout has nothing to do with outbound calls.
distractor_notes.D: Number Maintenance defines record numbering only.

rationale: IntegrationHub provides spokes and REST steps so flows can call external services without custom integration code.

stem: Which server-side automation runs automatically in response to database operations like insert or update?

options.text: A Business Rule
A Client Script
A UI Policy
A form view

distractor_notes.B: Client Scripts run in the browser on the form, not on database operations.
distractor_notes.C: UI Policies act on form fields client-side.
distractor_notes.D: A form view is a layout, not automation.

rationale: Business Rules execute server-side on database operations (insert, update, delete, query), making them core to record automation.

stem: You want reusable server-side functions that scripts and flows can call. What should you build?

options.text: A Script Include
An onLoad Client Script
A UI Action button
A form section

distractor_notes.B: Client Scripts run in the browser and are not reusable server libraries.
distractor_notes.C: UI Actions add controls to forms, not reusable server functions.
distractor_notes.D: A form section is a layout element.

rationale: Script Includes hold reusable server-side functions and classes that business rules, flows, and other scripts can call.

stem: What is the role of the staging (import set) table in a data import?

options.text: It temporarily holds incoming rows before transformation
It is the final destination for the data
It stores the transform map definition
It validates user roles for the import

distractor_notes.B: The target table is the final destination; the import set table is staging.
distractor_notes.C: Transform maps are separate configuration records.
distractor_notes.D: Role validation is handled by ACLs, not the staging table.

rationale: Import set tables stage raw incoming rows so a transform map can map and load them into the target table.

stem: What does a coalesce field do during a transform?

options.text: It matches incoming rows to existing records to update them
It deletes duplicate target records
It encrypts the imported values
It schedules the import to run nightly

distractor_notes.B: Coalescing updates or inserts; it does not delete duplicates.
distractor_notes.C: Coalesce has nothing to do with encryption.
distractor_notes.D: Scheduling is configured on the data source or import job.

rationale: A coalesce field is the key used to find a matching target record: a match updates the existing record, no match inserts a new one.

stem: An import keeps creating duplicate records instead of updating existing ones. What is the most likely fix?

options.text: Set an appropriate coalesce field in the transform map
Add more fields to the form layout
Grant the importing user the admin role
Increase the data source row limit

distractor_notes.B: Form layout doesn't affect insert-versus-update behavior.
distractor_notes.C: Admin rights don't change coalesce matching.
distractor_notes.D: Row limits change volume, not duplicate handling.

rationale: Without a coalesce field, every row inserts a new record; defining a coalesce key makes the transform update matching records instead.

stem: What does a data source define for an import?

options.text: Where the data comes from and its format
Which users may view the imported records
The form layout of the target table
The number format for new records

distractor_notes.B: Access to imported records is governed by ACLs.
distractor_notes.C: Form layout is unrelated to the data source.
distractor_notes.D: Numbering is set in Number Maintenance.

rationale: A data source specifies the origin (file, JDBC, REST) and format of the data to be loaded into an import set.

stem: You must map an incoming column to a reference field by display value rather than sys_id. What handles this?

options.text: A field map configured to use a referenced value/source script
A UI Policy on the target form
A coalesce on the staging table only
An ACL on the reference field

distractor_notes.B: UI Policies don't map import data to references.
distractor_notes.C: Coalesce identifies matching target records; it doesn't resolve display-to-reference mapping.
distractor_notes.D: ACLs control access, not field mapping logic.

rationale: Field maps in the transform map control how each source column maps to a target field, including referenced-value handling or source scripts to resolve references.

stem: What is the recommended way to move a custom application between instances when not using source control?

options.text: Publish the app to an update set and import it
Manually rebuild each record by hand
Copy the database directly
Email the XML of each record

distractor_notes.B: Manual rebuilding is error-prone and loses tracking.
distractor_notes.C: Direct database copies are not a supported app-transport method.
distractor_notes.D: Per-record XML email is unmanageable and not the standard process.

rationale: Publishing an application to an update set packages its files so they can be retrieved and committed on another instance.

stem: What does committing an update set on the target instance do?

options.text: Applies the captured changes to that instance
Deletes the update set permanently
Locks the source instance from edits
Publishes the app to the ServiceNow Store

distractor_notes.B: Committing applies changes; it does not delete the set.
distractor_notes.C: Committing does not lock the source instance.
distractor_notes.D: Store publishing is a separate process from committing an update set.

rationale: Committing a retrieved update set applies its captured configuration changes to the target instance.

stem: A change you made isn't moving with your update set. What is the most common reason?

options.text: The change is a data record not captured by update sets
The update set was never named
The target instance is offline
The change needs an admin to view it

distractor_notes.B: A missing name doesn't prevent capture of tracked changes.
distractor_notes.C: Instance availability isn't why a specific change is excluded.
distractor_notes.D: Visibility roles don't determine update set capture.

rationale: Update sets capture configuration changes, not most data records; data typically must be moved separately or via specified mechanisms.

stem: Where do you manage installed applications and plugins on an instance?

options.text: The Application Manager / All Apps page
The form designer
Number maintenance
The system dictionary

distractor_notes.B: The form designer arranges fields, not applications.
distractor_notes.C: Number Maintenance controls record numbering.
distractor_notes.D: The dictionary defines fields and tables.

rationale: Application Manager (All Apps) is where administrators install, upgrade, and manage applications and plugins.

stem: Before moving an app to production, you want automated regression tests of its core flows. Which ServiceNow tool fits?

options.text: Automated Test Framework (ATF)
The form designer
Number maintenance
A UI Policy

distractor_notes.B: The form designer builds layouts, not tests.
distractor_notes.C: Number Maintenance is unrelated to testing.
distractor_notes.D: UI Policies control form fields, not regression testing.

rationale: The Automated Test Framework lets you build and run repeatable tests so you can validate application behavior before promoting changes.
